review_notes: I read the whole file. I did not open the related sources, so the judgement rests on the file text alone. The Mon and Grp halves mirror each other: the two Small instances, shrinkYonedaMon and shrinkYonedaGrp, the two equivalences, and three lemmas each. The duplicated proofs are all single `simp [def, equiv]` calls or one-line `.symm` wrappers. These are short routine unfoldings and thin wrappers, which the rubric excludes. The two Small instances are `dsimp; infer_instance`. The Mon and Grp lemmas are about different functors (MonCat and GrpCat shrink functors) and different morphism types (`g.hom` versus `g.hom.hom`). A shared lemma would need an abstraction over both categories, and that would cost more than the duplicated one-liners. I found no nontrivial repeated reasoning that a shared lemma would improve.
